subject: maths
question: How many cuboid boxes of size 10 cm × 5 cm × 2 cm can be packed into a carton of size 50 cm × 25 cm × 20cm without leaving any space?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Number of boxes = (Length × Breadth × Height)Cₐᵣₜₒₙ ÷ (length × breadth × height)Bₒₓ

Number of boxes = (50 × 25 × 20) ÷ (10 × 5 × 2)

Number of boxes = 5 × 5 × 10 = 250

**∴ The correct answer is 250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1c7e83cf47ce9ea0b796f3949a6072ab24e774d85e4444880ccab90c876fa25.png] 

**Given:**

Dimensions of the **carton** (L, B, H) = 50 cm, 25 cm, 20 cm

Dimensions of the **cuboid box** (l, b, h) = 10 cm, 5 cm, 2 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a **cuboid** = Length × Breadth × Height

Number of objects = **Total Volume** ÷ **Volume of one object**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume of the **carton** = 50 cm × 25 cm × 20 cm

⇒ Volume of the **carton** = 25,000 cm³

⇒ Volume of one **cuboid box** = 10 cm × 5 cm × 2 cm

⇒ Volume of one **cuboid box** = 100 cm³

⇒ Number of boxes = 25,000 ÷ 100

⇒ Number of boxes = 250

**∴ The correct answer is 250.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cuboid

The total area covering the outer surface of a cuboid is given by TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl).

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid is its diagonal, calculated as D = √(l² + b² + h²).

Lateral Surface Area

The area of the four side walls (excluding top and bottom) is LSA = 2 × h × (l + b).</p
